There have been several encouraging numerical experiments (for this and other SDPs)

    There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that the Sum-of-Squares relaxation of degree 4 for the clique number of the Paley graph gives a bound of $O(p^{\frac12-\varepsilon})$.
target: For each prime p congruent to 1 modulo 4, let G_p have vertex set F_p, with distinct a,b adjacent exactly when a-b is a nonzero square. For a finite graph G on [n], define SOS_4(G) as the maximum of sum_i M_{empty,{i}} over a real positive-semidefinite matrix M indexed by subsets of [n] of size at most 2, subject to M_{empty,empty}=1, M_{S,T} depending only on S union T, and M_{S,T}=0 whenever S union T is not a clique of G. Prove that there exist fixed epsilon>0, C>0, and p0 such that SOS_4(G_p)<=C p^(1/2-epsilon) for every prime p>=p0 congruent to 1 modulo 4, or rigorously prove that this quantified statement is false.
title: Degree-four SoS improvement for Paley clique number
